input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of AMC Entertainment

ownership.value: Widely held public company listed on NYSE (ticker AMC); 892,604,638 Class A shares outstanding as of November 3, 2026. No controlling shareholder or PE sponsor: per the October 2025 proxy, the only >5% beneficial owners as of October 13, 2025 were Vanguard (5.95%), Discovery Capital Management (5.78%) and BlackRock (5.05%); directors/NEOs as a group hold well under 1% (CEO Adam Aron 975,310 shares). Former parent Wanda, which acquired AMC in 2012, sold most of its remaining shares via open-market sales in May 2021.

debt_events.summary: Closed a $3.97 billion refinancing covering ~97% of debt: issued $2,000.0M 8.875% First Lien Notes due 2031, borrowed $850.0M new first-lien term loans due 2031 (Wells Fargo agent) and $1,120.0M 11.25% second-lien term loans due 2033 (Deutsche Bank Special Situations Group); repaid in full the existing AMC term loan facility (July 2024 credit agreement) and the Odeon Term Loan Facility; settled the tender for 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2029 ($355,515,000 tendered, ~98.8% of $359,964,500 outstanding; remainder redeemable on/about Feb 15, 2027 at 100%); and redeemed in full Muvico's $903.4M Senior Secured Notes due 2029 at 100% plus a $144.3M make-whole premium.

Moody's detailed the refinancing plan: ~$3.7B of existing term loans and notes to be repaid (excluding ~$116M second-lien exchangeable notes due 2030 at Muvico), raising gross debt by over $170M but pushing weighted average maturity from ~3 years to ~6 years and cutting weighted average borrowing costs from ~11% toward ~9% pro forma.

Registered direct offering of 95,250,000 shares for ~$200M gross proceeds, used to call and redeem all $125,471,000 of 6.125% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2027 (redeemed July 24, 2026; ~$7.7M annual interest saved); ~$156M of exchangeable noteholders voluntarily converted into common stock; AMC said it anticipated no material debt principal repayments before 2029.

Closed the second liability-management transaction in a year ('LME 2.0') under the July 1, 2025 Transaction Support Agreement: ~$244.4M new-money financing from consenting 7.5% noteholders; $590.0M of 7.5% Senior Secured Notes due 2029 exchanged into $857.0M new Senior Secured Notes due Feb 19, 2029 (cash+PIK); at least $143.0M of 6.00%/8.00% Cash/PIK Toggle Senior Secured Exchangeable Notes due 2030 equitized into 79.8M shares; 2026 maturities (5.875% senior subordinated notes and 10%/12% Second Lien notes, ~$173.1M) redeemed; supported by ~90% of term loan lenders.

Settlement and mutual release dismissing with prejudice the intercreditor litigation A Holdings - B LLC, et al. v. GLAS Trust Company LLC and AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc., Case No. 654878/2024 (Sup. Ct. N.Y. Cnty. 2024), brought by holders of the legacy 7.5% 2029 notes over the 2024 transactions; credit agreement amended by required lenders to permit the transactions. Penalty-rate coupons (up to 9.50% cash + 3.50% PIK on new exchangeable notes) applied if shareholder approval for the underlying shares was not obtained by Dec 10, 2025.

credit_ratings.summary: S&P Global Ratings upgraded AMC Entertainment Holdings Inc. issuer credit rating to 'B-' from 'CCC+', outlook stable; issue ratings upgraded (first-lien term loan to 'B+', Muvico and 7.5% AMC secured notes to 'B-', Odeon first-lien term loan to 'B', exchangeable notes to 'CCC'). S&P assesses liquidity as adequate (sources exceed uses by >3.5x over next 12 months; nearest maturity 2029) but flags a highly leveraged financial risk profile: ~$3.8B debt, >$450M annual interest expense, $850M rent.

Fitch assigned AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc., Muvico LLC and Odeon Finco PLC first-time Long-Term IDRs of 'B-' with Positive Outlook; first-lien senior notes 'B-'/'RR4', senior secured term loan 'B'/'RR3', Muvico exchangeable notes 'CCC'/'RR6'. Leverage 6.5x EBITDA / 4.7x EBITDAR at 2Q26, down from 10.9x / 5.8x in Dec 2025; constrained by negative FCF over the last four years and a complex capital structure with an 86%-in-2029/2030 maturity wall management intends to address within 12-18 months.

Moody's upgraded AMC's Corporate Family Rating to B3 from Caa2 and changed outlook to positive from stable; Speculative Grade Liquidity rating upgraded to SGL-3 from SGL-4, on the refinancing plan (~$850M 1L term loan B due 2031, ~$2B 1L notes due 2031, ~$1.12B 2L term loans). Moody's expects leverage to decline toward the mid-to-low 4x range over 12-18 months and positive annual free cash flow in 2026 'for the first time in many years.'

Prior state before the 2026 upgrades: S&P kept AMC at issuer credit rating 'CCC+' with negative outlook while assigning a 'B-' issue rating ('2' recovery, ~85%) to the $857M senior secured notes due 2029 issued with Muvico LLC as co-borrower; S&P then viewed the capital structure as unsustainable with a ~$3.2B 2029 maturity wall, >$400M annual interest and $850M rent.

Context within ~28 months: S&P had lowered AMC to 'SD' (selective default) on announcement of the July 2024 distressed-exchange transaction - the first of two liability-management exercises in 12 months.

missing_fields: committed revolving credit facility / borrowed-capacity figure (no current revolver is disclosed in the Q3 2026 10-Q or rating-agency reports; liquidity is cash plus operating cash flow, and the 2013 $225M revolver and Tranche B loans relate to the legacy facility repaid in full on 2026-10-05)
auditor identity (no auditor change or going-concern qualification disclosed in reviewed filings)
output.risk_rationale: Elevated, though materially improved over the last 12 months. A $3.97 billion refinancing on October 5, 2026 covering ~97% of debt pushed maturities to 2031/2033 and triggered upgrades by all three agencies in under six weeks (S&P to B- on 2026-07-28, Fitch first-time B- positive on 2026-09-08, Moody's to B3 positive on 2026-09-21), while Q3 2026 revenue rose 31.6% to $1,711.1M with record adjusted EBITDA of $347.5M. However, AMC still carries roughly $4 billion of debt (Moody's pro forma gross debt $4,139M) against a $(1,343.1)M stockholders' deficit, pays over $450M annual interest plus $850M rent (S&P), funds itself partly with serial equity issuances ($333.6M in 9M 2026 plus a $200M June 2026 direct offering), and its own 10-Q states historical cash burn rates are 'not sustainable long-term' with no assurance of liquidity beyond twelve months. The 2024-2025 distressed exchanges (S&P 'SD' in July 2024, LME 2.0 in July 2025) and an 11.25% second-lien tranche from Deutsche Bank underline that cheap capital remains unavailable; full-year 2026 free-cash-flow positivity would be the first in many years (Moody's).

distress_signals.summary: Q3 2026 10-Q liquidity language: AMC believes existing cash plus operating cash flow is sufficient through the next twelve months, but states 'The Company's historical cash burn rates are not sustainable long-term' and 'There can be no assurances that the Company will be successful in generating the additional liquidity necessary to meet the Company's obligations beyond twelve months.'

Standing risk-factor language in the Q3 2026 10-Q: if unable to generate sustainable annual net positive operating cash flows and additional liquidity is not obtained or insufficient, AMC 'likely would seek an in-court or out-of-court restructuring of our liabilities', and equity holders would likely suffer a total loss in liquidation.

Continued fleet downsizing: three theater closures in Q3 2026; 228 locations closed versus 66 opened since 2020 (net reduction of 159 theaters since 2020 per S&P) under a multiyear optimization program.

Fitch flags structural constraints: negative free cash flow over the last four years, high absolute debt with weak interest coverage, liquidity sensitive to seasonal swings and high fixed-cost obligations, and a complex multi-tiered capital structure requiring creditor consents for refinancing; a large maturity wall (~86% of debt maturing 2029, exchangeable notes 2030, Odeon term loan 2031) that management intends to address in the next 12-18 months.

No auditor change, going-concern qualification, CFO or other senior executive departure found in the reviewed filings and press for the last 12 months; CFO Sean Goodman remained in office through the Q3 2026 earnings call, and the 10-Q contains no going-concern qualification (management affirming 12-month sufficiency) and no default under Item 3 'Defaults Upon Senior Securities'.

payment_behaviour.summary: Creditor-dispute history (not supplier payment): bondholder litigation over the 2024 distressed-exchange transactions - A Holdings - B LLC et al. v. GLAS Trust Company LLC and AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc., Case No. 654878/2024 (NY Sup. Ct.) - was dismissed with prejudice in July 2025 under a settlement with mutual releases, and litigation with holders of the 7.5% Senior Secured Notes due 2029 was fully resolved.

No current supplier liens, collection suits, judgments, missed payments or late-payment reports against AMC Entertainment Holdings were found in the court records and filings reviewed for the last 12 months; the Q3 2026 10-Q discloses no default under Item 3 'Defaults Upon Senior Securities', and scheduled interest and redeemed notes were paid in cash on their due dates (e.g., $125.5M subordinated notes redeemed July 24, 2026; $355.5M tender paid October 5, 2026).
